# XMP sidecars and interchange

LightCraft keeps its catalog as the source of truth, and can also store each photo's metadata and develop settings in
an XMP sidecar next to the original. Sidecars let edits travel with the files (backups, another LightCraft library,
other tools), and let LightCraft pick up edits made elsewhere.

## Sidecar files

| | |
|---|---|
| Name | `<stem>.xmp` by default (`IMG_0001.CR3` → `IMG_0001.xmp`); `<file>.xmp` (`IMG_0001.CR3.xmp`) with `naming: "full"`. Reading accepts either (preferred first) and `.XMP`. With stem naming, files sharing a stem don't share a sidecar: see *Shared names* below. |
| Write | `photo.saveMetadataToFile {ids?}` (Photo ▸ Save Metadata to File, ⌘S), or automatically after every change with `library.xmpPreferences {autoWrite: true}` (File ▸ Automatically Write Changes into XMP). Slider drags are written once, when the drag ends; undo/redo rewrite the sidecar. An existing sidecar is **merged into, never replaced** (see *Saving into an existing sidecar*). Written atomically (temp file, fsync, rename). The result lists `written`, `merged` and `backups`. |

`Interop/lightroom-index.json` records imported identities. Source catalogs and originals are
never overwritten.

Native import is bounded to a 1 GiB database/WAL, 16 MiB XMP packets and one million rows per
table. The in-tree, read-only Rust SQLite B-tree reader follows SQLite’s public file-format
specification; it introduces no dependency or C runtime. Table payloads are capped at 256 MiB.
Optional history, keyword and collection tables that exceed limits are skipped with warnings;
required photo tables still report errors. Unrelated unsupported schemas are ignored. A needed
WITHOUT ROWID or virtual table produces an explicit error, handled as a warning when optional.

Develop settings reuse the existing XMP/preset mapper. Supported sliders, curves and supported
mask structures remain editable, but this is approximate rendering: camera profiles, Adobe AI
models, some masking/retouch fields and process-version algorithms are not reproduced. Unmapped
fields are reported. When a recovery archive is saved, it retains source settings/history/snapshots
and original smart-collection rules. Smart collections become regular albums with current
membership. Archived history and snapshots are source data, not native LightCraft history yet.

**[STU-RAS-159] BLEND-IF RANGE MODEL — EIGHT VALUES PER CHANNEL, NOT FOUR.** A blend range is stored per
channel as **eight** values, not four: source black start, source black end, source white start,
source white end, and the same four for the destination. The paired values are what make a Blend-If
slider *split* and feather; collapsing each pair to one number turns every split slider into a hard
cut. Every value is in `levels_0_255` with hard bounds 0..255 (`declared`). The defaults are
`source_black = (0, 0)`, `source_white = (255, 255)`, `destination_black = (0, 0)`,
`destination_white = (255, 255)` — that is, the identity range — and these are `derived`. A blend-range
entry additionally carries a channel reference, so the set is per-channel and the composite gray entry
is one member of it, not a separate mechanism.

Canonical primitive addition: `StudioRawDevelop` (schema id `hsk.studio.raw_develop@1`) joins the canonical Studio primitive set of [STU-DOC-002] alongside `StudioLayer`, `StudioMask`, `StudioSelectionSet`, `StudioAdjustment`, and `StudioColorProfile`; its field-level definition is owned by 14.23 and referenced (not redefined) here. All raw develop state is durable Studio authority under the SurrealDB/EventLedger contract of [STU-ARC-004] — there is no XMP sidecar file, no private raw-develop database, and no SQLite cache; the "non-destructive settings storage" behavior of the source suites is satisfied by the EventLedger + authority-record model, not by an external metadata file.

**[STU-ASSET-019] Catalog capability set inherited by Studio.** Studio's asset projection inherits, and MUST NOT re-implement, the catalog capabilities defined for the Library/DAM surface at Spec 10.10.4.5: import by copy, import by reference in place, import by move, content-hash duplicate detection, hierarchical keyword tagging, 0-to-5 star rating, colour labels, pick/reject/unflagged flags, manual collections, rule-based smart collections, filesystem folder synchronisation, EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata read and write, face-region tagging and identity clustering, geotagging and map view, image stacking, and virtual copies. Where a Studio workflow needs one of these, it calls it; it does not rebuild it.

Cull with active-photo versus all-selected metadata scope
Maintain hierarchical keywords, stacks, manual and rule collections

Develop selected fields only, retain per-photo masks/crops
Export selected variants with explicit profile, size, sharpening, naming and metadata policy
workflows.counterexample: A collapsed stack and filtered grid show 40 thumbnails from 500 canonical photos; all-collection export must not silently target only loaded rows.
workflows.proof: Canonical membership read before/after; materialized variant hashes; independent export metadata/profile inspection; Argus active/selected scope and hidden-stack state.

workflows.name: Legacy RAW re-edit and deterministic migration
steps: Read RAW identity, EXIF orientation, originating process and camera/lens profile references
Preserve old tone controls and immutable source settings
Apply non-AI brush, radial, linear and range masks with add/subtract/intersect/invert
Explicitly migrate process version with before/after receipt
Render and reopen using pinned renderer/profile dependencies
workflows.counterexample: Legacy Exposure/Contrast/Blacks preset is converted to modern controls while ProcessVersion is treated as bookkeeping; labels and slider numbers survive but the look and future edit behavior change.
workflows.proof: Compare independent source-authored renders and typed state for old/new process versions, unsupported-profile status, panel enable flags, crop/orientation and ordered masks; reject silent version conversion.

workflows.name: Disconnected original editing
steps: Build a bounded derived preview linked to immutable original identity
Disconnect original storage
Edit variant parameters
Reattach or relink original
Render full-resolution delivery with retained edit graph
workflows.counterexample: Preview itself is promoted as the full-resolution original; reconnect duplicates variants or applies the develop stack twice.
workflows.proof: Independent original digest before/after; missing-original and proxy-resolution UI state; identical edit graph through reconnect; explicit delivery limit when original remains absent.

workflows.name: Layered retouch and linked commercial composite
steps: Open developed RAW as re-editable placed source
Create shared embedded instances and independent copies
Link another asset across two documents
Apply transformations, masks and Smart Filters
Blend current/underlying channels with split thresholds, fill/opacity and knockout
Save PSD/PSB, close, reopen and modify placed source
workflows.counterexample: An opaque SoLd block survives byte round-trip while the imported layer is only a flattened preview; updating source then fails to update intended instances.
workflows.proof: Two-document and two-instance update behavior; source edit after reopen; masks/filter graph state; missing-link recovery; independent render against reference with high-bit-depth gradient and layer effects.

workflows.name: Color-managed print variant
steps: Keep wide-gamut master
Choose printer/paper proof profile and rendering intent
Inspect monitor and output gamut warnings
Create proof variant
Adjust proof variant without mutating master
Export with profile/intent and inspect delivery
workflows.counterexample: Proof profile is assigned to pixels instead of applied as a view transform; original changes when proof copy is edited.
workflows.proof: Master state invariant; proof variant relation; ICC/profile digest, intent and paper/ink flags; independent color-managed render and output metadata, not screenshot-only similarity.

workflows.name: Lightroom versus Classic migration
steps: Identify whether source is Classic catalog, Local directory/XMP, cloud original or cloud Smart Preview
Read complete eligible canonical source set
Preserve separate local/cloud identities and edits
Transfer catalog-only variants/history/rules via file-byte importer when available
Report unsupported or missing artifacts per item
workflows.counterexample: A cloud sync export is presented as a complete Classic migration even though histories, snapshots and keywords never crossed the sync boundary.
workflows.proof: Source-channel capability matrix and per-item reconciliation; missing source fields are explicit, never synthesized; no cloud runtime dependency or second catalog authority.

workflows.name: Multi-artboard commercial PDF delivery
